items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Chet Baker as a 'great white hope' and 'superstar' in the context of discussing white musicians in jazz, but the interviewee (Sam Jones) does not respond with any personal anecdote, collaboration, or direct interaction with Chet Baker.

ctx.x: I have to talk about the laymen men because he's the man that takes care of us, you know. So these writers started writing about these freedom players, you see. And yeah, I do believe that it was a conspiracy and that because in order for the white musician to get a play, they had to get all these people off the scene man because there wasn't too much places for white musicians to play. Who did you have? Gerry Mulligan, the Superstars, at that time that boy played the trumpet.

Chet Baker and he was a great white hope, singing and playing the trumpet. You got your great Stan Getz. He was your next great white hope, you see. People like Zoot Sims, you know he was mentioned but he wasn't a big star like those guys was, you know. Who else? Like I say, you can count those guys, those white guys on your one hand. Those were your big white superstars in jazz, Bob Brookmeyer, he was mentioned but he wasn't a superstar.
